task.description: Implement the validated design at src/design/iss0617-gbl134-missing-tables-followup.md -- a NEW forward migration GBL-136 (next available GBL-<NNN> number after GBL-135; check ls migrations/GBL-* to confirm) that drops tenant_default shadow copies of exactly 8 GLOBAL_REGISTRY tables: artifact_versions, event_type_registry_producers, oidc_migration_item, oidc_migration_job, registry_idp_operation_ledger, repository_artifacts, tenant, tenant_hostnames. This is a git-setup-already-done run (branch feature/WF03-GH566-20260808 exists and is checked out) -- do NOT run git-setup again, only implement + commit. Read the full design doc before starting -- it specifies: (1) the same safety pattern as GBL-134 (existence checks, RESTRICT mode, per-tenant-schema loop), (2) drop tenant_hostnames before tenant (FK ordering), (3) artifact_versions will ALWAYS fail its RESTRICT drop (legitimate PER_TENANT tables artifact_activations/artifact_activation_history and repository_form_schemas all FK into it) -- this is CORRECT, expected, permanent behavior, not a bug to work around; (4) each table's DROP TABLE must be wrapped in its own BEGIN...EXCEPTION WHEN dependent_objects_still_exist...END block so artifact_versions's expected failure does not abort the other 7 tables' drops -- this is a genuine, validated deviation from GBL-134's bare structure, not an invented pattern. Do NOT include the 5 tables (api_token_audit, event_payload_store, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_waits, variable_schemas) that GBL-135 already resolved in the opposite direction -- including them would be a regression. Do NOT include the 4 tables ISS-0620 flagged as misclassified (artifact_activation_groups, entity_definitions, entity_record_latest, entity_type_instances) -- that is a separate, unresolved issue, out of scope here.
acceptance_criteria: New migration file created following the GBL-<NNN>_iss0617_... naming convention
Exactly the 8 validated table names in scope -- no more, no less
Each DROP TABLE wrapped in its own exception-handling block per the validated design
artifact_versions is confirmed to fail its drop gracefully (logged, not aborting the migration)
zig build migrate exits 0 against a freshly migrated database
TC-EXP-601-01 through 04 -- confirm which now pass (design notes TC-EXP-601-04s instance_waits-related failure mode is NOT fixed by this migration, only the repository_artifacts-caused failures)
No production Zig code touched -- this is a migration-only fix
